front: The points in a scatterplot fall close to a line that slopes downward from left to right. How do you describe the association?
back: A strong negative linear association: as $x$ increases, $y$ tends to decrease, and the points stay close to a line. Points spread widely around the line would make it weak; a curved pattern would make it nonlinear.
reason: The correlation coefficient r is not on the digital SAT; association is described in words.

back: A point that falls far from the general pattern of the data, far from the line of best fit, so it has a large residual. An outlier can change the slope and intercept of the line of best fit and make the association look weaker.
reason: Drop the correlation coefficient; keep residuals.
